task: Implement the Product Owner approved Loot Vault v2 design direction within the existing Template Factory and Visual Builder contracts, preserving shared platform authorities.
notes: Product Owner approved the Loot Vault v2 Visual First direction on 2026-09-28. This branch is reconciled onto canonical main e728c3a58b531234a420576d74b2a6e68e65ec53, including PR #482 Template Production Contracts Foundation. LOOT_VAULT_V2_GENERATOR_BLUEPRINT remains the structural and production-contract authority for recipe identity, required capabilities, canonical 14-page composition, shared Page Schema/component/runtime/Visual Builder ownership, Desktop/Tablet/Mobile authority, Visual Authority, file ownership, and compiled component-usage evidence. The #482 mechanisms are preserved; its Visual Authority declaration is aligned to the later Product Owner-approved 2026-09-28 Visual First reference across all 14 canonical pages. The Blueprint must not replace or simplify the approved Visual First design. Shared renderer changes are restricted to generic platform capabilities such as cinematic-commerce and the explicitly scoped tablet navigation disclosure in storefront-commerce-header; no Loot Vault-specific commerce/auth/account/checkout runtime branch is permitted. Candidate-only until exact-head Generator Readiness, Production Contracts, Factory, responsive 14x3, interaction, build, and visual fidelity proof pass. No golden, staging, main, or production promotion is implied. Product Owner completed the mobile visual/functional audit on 2026-09-29. Implementation order is now P0 shared commerce preview/runtime continuity first, then shared navigation/icon consistency, then page-specific content/media fixes. The template showroom must demonstrate variant selection, add-to-cart acknowledgement, cart quantity/remove, checkout shipping/payment selection, and fail-closed order submission. Preview/demo behavior may not create a real order. Product Owner also reaffirmed the activation rule: when the merchant explicitly opens/publishes the webshop, a confirmation must explain which demo content will be removed; demo cleanup semantics must be finalized before activation work is completed. The PO audit record is intentionally stored outside docs/support so the historical incident backfill does not misclassify an active acceptance checklist as an unresolved support incident. Atlas scope explicitly classifies the shared add-to-cart confirmation as storefront presentation; it does not grant storefront ownership of cart/order truth. The P0 implementation changes storefront preview integration, not Commerce Core transactional truth, so commerce-runtime is intentionally not declared as a changed subsystem; DOMAIN-QUALITY is declared only because the canonical Atlas mapping itself was updated. PO content cleanup uses one shared presentation primitive (content.accordion) and canonical Page Schema edits; no template-local interaction engine is introduced. Legal preview routes preserve document identity through demoContent slugs. Header utility actions now carry semantic favorites/account/cart kinds so preview URL rewriting cannot degrade their canonical SVG identity. The shared account auth trigger receives the already-authorized target href instead of hard-coding /fiokom, preserving template-preview continuity.
